Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd Launches New High-Efficiency Copper Anode

Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd, a prominent player in Zambia’s growing metals and mining sector, announced the launch of its latest product: a high-efficiency copper anode designed to meet the evolving demands of global manufacturers and electronics producers. The new product, unveiled at a ceremony at the firm’s facility in the Copperbelt Province on Thursday, promises enhanced conductivity and reduced impurities, positioning Chambishi to capitalize on rising demand for refined copper.

“This is a significant milestone for Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd, and for Zambia’s mining industry as a whole,” said Managing Director Mutale Mwanza during the launch event. “Our new anode leverages advanced refining technology to deliver copper that meets the rigorous quality standards of international markets. It reflects our commitment to innovation and sustainability.”

According to the company, the new copper anode achieves impurity levels as low as 0.01%, which is below the typical industry average of 0.03%. Company engineers highlighted the adoption of proprietary electro-refining processes which, they say, both reduce energy consumption and maximize yield.

Industry analysts note that the launch comes at an opportune time, with global copper demand projected to rise 4% annually through 2027, fueled by the energy transition and increased investment in electric infrastructure. “Zambia is already Africa’s second-largest copper producer, and initiatives like this help maintain the country’s competitiveness,” said Chola Mwaba, an analyst at Lusaka-based investment firm Zambezi Wealth Partners.

The Zambia Chamber of Mines welcomed the development. “Value addition and technological upgrades are essential for the sector’s growth,” said Chamber spokesperson Felix Simbeye. “Products like Chambishi’s new copper anode enable local firms to access higher-value export markets.”

Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd indicated that the product is already being trialed by several downstream partners, including wire and cable manufacturers and electronics firms in Asia and Europe. The company plans to ramp up production to an initial 30,000 tonnes per annum, with expansion potential if demand continues to strengthen.
